source.title: Nexus: Same Pretraining Loss, Better Downstream Generalization via Common Minima
source.authors: Huan-Ran Chen; Hua-Qing Zhang; Xiao Li; Yin-Peng Dong; Ke Shen; Jun Zhu

record.file_problem: Text contains the full paper and appendices; no apparent truncation or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: Compares training methods and measures pretraining and downstream outcomes, including matched-pretraining-loss comparisons. It does not test memorization of random labels or the other specific interventions in most claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study's results concern LLM pretraining with Nexus, a gradient-similarity regularizer, and downstream benchmarks. Rows capture its own reported comparisons and measurements. Cited prior work and hyperparameter values used only to select settings are not rows.
record.test_reason: Appendix D.8 tests batch size in a new language-model setting: AdamW batches 128 and 256 use approximately matched token budgets, with twice as many stable and decay steps for batch 128. The larger batch performs better. The main Nexus comparisons do not test any listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase captures the main conclusion: Nexus encourages gradient and parameter closeness and generally improves downstream performance at nearly matched pretraining validation loss. Qualify robustness: individual metrics can worsen, excessive regularization harms performance, and the authors explicitly report incompatibility with Muon. They also acknowledge that closeness and flatness may be coupled, leaving their separate contributions unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: Adds Nexus gradient-similarity regularization through an inner normalized-SGD trajectory; tested mainly with AdamW as the outer optimizer. The paper also compares Muon and a Muon-inspired SGDM setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome varies with Nexus inner learning rate γ: γ = 0.40 increases pretraining loss and reduces average downstream accuracy. Reported downstream gains also vary by data mixture, model size, schedule, and training duration.

fits_no_version.finding: Nexus improves downstream performance at nearly unchanged pretraining validation loss; the 3B comparison gives average accuracy 40.3% versus 37.1%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Explicit gradient-similarity regularization can improve downstream LLM performance at matched pretraining validation loss.

fits_no_version.finding: Nexus increases gradient similarity and reduces leading Hessian eigenvalues; the top eigenvalue at step 50k is 1.609 versus 8.330.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Nexus changes gradient alignment and unscaled curvature during LLM pretraining, with their separate contributions to downstream performance unresolved.

fits_no_version.finding: Nexus gains vary with regularization strength, data mixture, model size, and fine-tuning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The downstream benefits of Nexus depend on training conditions and can persist after supervised fine-tuning.

record.problems: The study concerns LLM pretraining and downstream benchmark outcomes rather than the random-label/image-classifier settings in the claim. Several reported comparisons are single runs; multi-seed results use only three 1B runs and two 3B runs with the same data order. The authors state that closeness and flatness may be coupled, so their separate contributions remain unclear. Public-dataset results have benchmark contamination concerns.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were omitted for the 60-row limit. Some benchmark-by-benchmark table entries and ablations are not separately extracted where the reported aggregate comparison captures the principal result; Appendix D.7–D.9 contains additional SGDM, batch-size, and regularization-strength results, but these do not test a listed claim version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out performance.
Convolutional versus fully connected image architectures and learned locality.

Controlled adaptive-optimizer versus standard SGD comparisons under limited or broader tuning, switching optimizers, and decoupled-weight-decay recovery. The modified SGDM ablation primarily compares SGDM with SGDM plus Nexus.
Batch sizes beyond an identified workload-dependent threshold; a broad batch-size sweep; longer-training recovery and learning-rate or normalization adaptations for large batches.
Dropout interventions, small-data failure, excessive-dropout underfitting, and joint removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, training–test generalization gaps, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Influence-based identification and removal of memorized training examples followed by retraining.

missing.what: Add batch-128 versus batch-256 AdamW comparisons for each model size. At 1B, pretraining/OOD losses are 1.937/1.506 versus 1.826/1.433, and average accuracy is 17.0% versus 21.9%. At 3B, losses are 1.627/1.326 versus 1.606/1.302, and accuracy is 34.8% versus 37.1%. Record the doubled stable and decay step counts for batch 128. Although rows_left_out mentions this experiment, its assertion that it bears on no version needs correction.
missing.locator: Appendix D.8; Table 13 versus Table 2; Figure 11

record.verdict_notes: No existing row directly measures a listed version, so their states are cannot_determine relative to those versions. The batch-size appendix supplies the V5 evidence. Its reversal over batches 128–256 qualifies scope rather than refuting a penalty beyond an unidentified larger-batch threshold.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization on the specified image datasets and models.
Width sweeps across the interpolation threshold in one-hidden-layer ReLU networks.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
The reported optimizer comparisons do not test whether adaptive optimizers generalize worse than SGD under limited tuning, nor the listed recovery conditions or word-level language-model exception.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and the listed recipe adaptations.
Dropout and weight-decay interventions in the specified image-classification regimes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.

relationships.display_finding: Higher average accuracy at batch 256 was reported for both model sizes, but these comparisons remain unverified and identify no harmful batch threshold.

relation.reason: The study experimentally varies batch size and reports downstream performance, although its tested range does not establish V5's large-batch regime.

tranche.reason: Appendix D.8 directly compares batch sizes in a new LLM-pretraining setting relevant to V5. The main Nexus comparisons measure different constructs.
